what: Check 92, part A: the 51 signals of study 90 coded a second time, blind, by three convened readers (CODEBOOK92.md, part A), as each wrote its file. Texts in sources92.json.

signals.reasons: Threshold is a number: Art 51(2) '10^25' floating point operations. Deadline 'without delay and in any event within two weeks' = 336 h from 'that requirement is met or it becomes known that it will be met'.
signals.doubt: Art 52(6) has the Commission publish a list of systemic-risk models; I coded the notice itself as not public (list names models only, not the notification). Clock could be read as awareness ('becomes known').

signals.receiver_name: AI Office and national competent authorities
signals.reasons: Content set by Annex XI; handed over only 'upon request'; Art 53(7)/55(3) treat it under Art 78 confidentiality. Art 55(1)(a) adversarial-testing documentation merged here (same receiver, same occasion).
signals.doubt: Art 55(1)(a) documentation has no stated receiver; I treated it as part of the on-request package. Retention not stated for the provider (10 years in Art 54(3)(b) binds the authorised representative only).

signals.receiver_name: providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the model
signals.reasons: Annex XII sets minimum elements; must 'enable providers of AI systems to have a good understanding of the capabilities and limitations'. Not published.
signals.doubt: Kind fits 'evaluation' only loosely (capability description); trigger could be 'schedule' (keep up to date) rather than before deployment.

signals.receiver_name: AI Office and, as appropriate, national competent authorities
signals.reasons: 'serious incident' defined in Art 3(49): incident or malfunctioning leading to death, serious harm to health, critical infrastructure disruption, fundamental-rights infringement. Deadline 'without undue delay'; no starting point named.
signals.doubt: Art 3(49) text in the file lists (a)-(c); Art 73 elsewhere has (d) property/environment, out of scope here. Clock coded none because none is stated.

signals.reasons: 'within five business days of either being confirmed' = 168 h; content defined by Measure 1.1. Measure 10.2 has Signatories publish a summarised Framework, so public (summary).
signals.doubt: Trigger could be 'before deployment' (Framework confirmed at latest two weeks before placing on market, Measure 1.1). Public is a summary, with removals and an exception for similarly-safe models.

signals.reasons: Access 'by the time they place a model on the market' (0 h); updates 'within five business days' (168 h); 'delay ... by up to 15 business days' = 360 h maximum, with an interim report 'without delay'. Measure 10.2 publishes a summarised Model Report incl. 'high-level descriptions of the systemic risk assessment results'.
signals.doubt: Shortest/longest: 0 and 360; the 168 h update deadline sits between. Six-monthly update (Measure 7.6) treated as the same signal.

signals.receiver_name: AI Office and, as applicable, national competent authorities
signals.retention: at least five years from the date of the documentation or of the incident, whichever is later (Measure 9.4)
signals.reasons: Initial reports 2 days (48 h) / 5 / 10 / 15 days (360 h) 'after the Signatories become aware of the involvement of their model'; final report 'not later than 60 days after the serious incident has been resolved' (1440 h); updates every four weeks. Class '(self-)exfiltration of model weights' is the model's own conduct.
signals.doubt: Longest deadline: initial-report maximum is 360 h; I took the final report (1440 h) as the text's longest. Machine_or_person 'by class' rests on the self-exfiltration class; other classes only say 'involvement of their model'. Incident reports are not in Measure 10.2, so not public.

signals.retention: at least 10 years after the model has been placed on the market (Measure 10.1)
signals.reasons: Items (1)-(4) listed incl. 'detailed description of the model evaluations ... including their results'; 'upon request'; 'retained at least 10 years'.

signals.receiver_name: the Signatory, or the AI Office and national competent authorities
signals.reasons: Signatory 'facilitate[s] the reporting ... by downstream modifiers, downstream providers, users, and other third parties', 'by informing such third parties of direct reporting channels, if available'. Reportable class is serious incidents (Commitment 9 / glossary).
signals.doubt: Receiver is either the Signatory (own record) or the AI Office; coded public body. Reporter is the third party, the signatory's duty is to facilitate.

extra.passage: Signatories will publish (e.g. via their websites) a summarised version of their Framework and Model Report(s), and updates thereof
extra.why: Own publication occasion to the public, with its own receiver (public) and trigger ('if and insofar as necessary to assess and/or mitigate systemic risks'); distinct from the AI Office notices COP1/COP2. Could be folded into those two.

extra.passage: keep a copy of the technical documentation specified in Annex XI at the disposal of the AI Office and national competent authorities, for a period of 10 years
extra.why: Record-keeping with a 10-year retention, but the duty is the authorised representative's (third-country providers); it parallels EU2. Borderline for inclusion.

extra.passage: procure any such independent external evaluators to provide the requisite information directly to the AI Office at the same time that the Signatory supplies its Model Report
extra.why: Separate reporter (external evaluators) sending evaluation-access information to the AI Office; may count as part of COP2.

extra.passage: provide a sufficiently large number of random samples of inputs and outputs from a relevant model evaluation if subsequently asked by the AI Office
extra.why: On-request evaluation outputs to the AI Office; may be folded into COP4/COP2.

signals.reasons: Operators of systems whose 'cumulative computing amount used for learning meets or exceeds' the Decree standard 'shall submit the results of implementing the measures'; no date or content is fixed (Minister sets guidelines, Art. 32(3)). Measures are risk identification/assessment/mitigation, so kind=evaluation.
signals.doubt: Trigger: the text gives no timing, only a compute threshold; coded 'before deployment' per the codebook's 'threshold is met in development'. 'schedule' is the alternative. Unit: results are named, what qualifies is left to guidelines and a Decree not in the text.

signals.reasons: The Minister 'may require that AI business operators submit relevant data' only where a violation is found or suspected or a report or complaint is received (Art. 40(1)); sets a duty on operators once required.
signals.doubt: Kind is a forced fit ('relevant data' about compliance with Arts. 31(2)-(3), 32, 34(1)); evaluation chosen, log or inventory arguable. Whether this is a signal or a body's own power is a borderline call; the duty to submit once required is read as a duty on the operator.

signals.reasons: Large frontier developer must publish the framework ('clearly and conspicuously ... on its internet website'), review it yearly, and 'publish the modified frontier AI framework and a justification ... within 30 days' of a material modification. 30 days = 720 h.
signals.doubt: Initial publication has no stated deadline; only the 30-day modification deadline is coded.

signals.reasons: 'Before, or concurrently with, deploying' a new or substantially modified frontier model: transparency report; large developers add summaries of catastrophic-risk assessments and their results. Latest permitted moment is deployment, so 0 h.
signals.doubt: deadline 0 is the 'concurrently' bound; kind chosen as evaluation because of the assessment summaries, the rest of the report is model facts (languages, uses).

signals.reasons: 'transmit to the Office of Emergency Services a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk resulting from internal use ... every three months'; reports 'exempt from the California Public Records Act' (22757.13(f)); only an anonymised annual aggregate of incident reports is produced, not of these.
signals.doubt: 'Three months' taken at its longest, 92 days = 2208 h; the text also allows 'another reasonable schedule specified by the ... developer', which is unbounded and not coded.

signals.reasons: 'report any critical safety incident ... within 15 days of discovering'. Critical safety incident (22757.11(d)) includes a model that 'uses deceptive techniques against the frontier developer' with no harm needed, and loss of control: model conduct as class. OES annual report is 'anonymized and aggregated' (22757.13(g)).
signals.doubt: Trigger mixed: classes (1)-(3) need death, injury or harm; class (4) does not, so coded 'event short of harm'. The OES report goes to the Legislature and Governor; read as aggregate only, not as full publication.

signals.receiver_name: an appropriate authority, including a law enforcement or public safety agency with jurisdiction (not one named body)
signals.reasons: 'discovers that a critical safety incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury ... disclose that incident within 24 hours to an authority'. Imminent risk of death is read as likely harm.
signals.doubt: Trigger harm vs event short of harm: the incident class includes the no-harm deception case, but the imminent-risk condition makes harm likely. Receiver is a class of authority, no named body; whether that is a 'named' public body is arguable. Not a separate publication path.

signals.reasons: OES 'shall establish a mechanism to be used by a frontier developer or a member of the public to report a critical safety incident' with date, reasons, short statement, and whether tied to internal use. Reports exempt from public records law; annual anonymised aggregate only.
signals.doubt: The duty to build the channel is the body's; coded as a signal because the channel fixes what persons report. Trigger follows the same mixed incident class as CA4. The field 'associated with internal use' is not an actor field, so machine_or_person is 'by class', not 'required'.

signals.receiver_name: Attorney General (also a federal authority, a person with authority over the employee, or another covered employee with authority to correct)
signals.reasons: Developer 'shall not ... prevent a covered employee from disclosing' to the Attorney General where there is reasonable cause to believe of a 'specific and substantial danger ... from a catastrophic risk' or a violation. AG's annual report is 'anonymized and aggregated' (22757.14(d)); employee reports exempt from public records.
signals.doubt: This is a non-obstruction duty, not a duty to report; coded as the packet lists it. The reportable content (danger or violation) does not name the model as actor, so 'not addressed', although catastrophic risk includes model conduct.

signals.receiver_name: the large frontier developer (internal process); disclosures and responses shared with officers and directors
signals.reasons: 'provide a reasonable internal process through which a covered employee may anonymously disclose'; 'a monthly update to the person who made the disclosure'; disclosures 'shared with officers and directors ... at least once each quarter'.
signals.doubt: Two schedules for one signal: monthly update to the discloser (31 days = 744 h) and quarterly sharing with officers (92 days = 2208 h). Receiver is the reporter's own employer, coded 'own record'; 'other party' arguable.

signals.reasons: Publish the framework; 'publish the modified frontier AI framework and a justification for that modification within thirty days' of a material modification; yearly review. 30 days = 720 h.
signals.doubt: Initial publication has no stated deadline. Applies from 2027-01-01.

signals.reasons: 'Before, or concurrently with, deploying' a new or substantially modified frontier model, publish a transparency report; large developers include summaries of catastrophic-risk assessments and results (1421(3)(b)).
signals.doubt: Same coding as CA2; 0 h is the 'concurrently' bound.

signals.receiver_name: the office (within the department of financial services)
signals.reasons: 'shall transmit to the office a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk resulting from internal use ... every three months'; such reports 'are exempt from disclosure' (1422(6)).
signals.doubt: Three months at the longest, 92 days = 2208 h; an 'another reasonable schedule ... agreed upon by the office' option exists and is not coded.

signals.receiver_name: the office (within the department of financial services)
signals.reasons: 'within seventy-two hours from a determination that a critical safety incident has occurred' or from learning facts giving 'reasonable belief'. Class (1420(4)) includes model deception with no harm, and loss of control. Annual office report is 'anonymized and aggregated' (1422(7)), from 2028.
signals.doubt: Trigger mixed, as CA4. Clock is awareness (determination or reasonable belief). Reports exempt from public records law (1422(6)).

signals.receiver_name: an appropriate authority, including a law enforcement or public safety agency with jurisdiction (not one named body)
signals.reasons: 'discovers that a critical safety incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury ... disclose that incident within twenty-four hours to an authority'.
signals.doubt: Same as CA5: harm vs event short of harm, and a class of authority rather than a named body.

signals.receiver_name: the office (within the department of financial services)
signals.reasons: 'The office shall establish a mechanism to be used by a frontier developer or a member of the public to report a critical safety incident' with date, reasons, statement, internal-use flag; reports exempt from disclosure; annual anonymised aggregate only.
signals.doubt: Body's duty to set up a channel, coded as a signal like CA6.

signals.receiver_name: the office (within the department of financial services)
signals.reasons: 'no large frontier developer may develop, deploy, or operate a frontier model ... without having a current disclosure statement filed'; 'renewed every two years, whenever ownership ... is transferred or ... a material change'. The office 'shall maintain and publish a list' of filers, without contact details.
signals.doubt: Public: only the list of filers (identity) is published, not the statement; coded 'public' as a minimal summary of each filing, 'not public' arguable. Deadlines: before developing (0 h) and two-year renewal at its longest, 731 days = 17544 h; earlier of ownership transfer or material change has no number.

signals.reasons: 'Reports ... are due no later than the first business day of the month following the transaction.' Content fixed in 743.10(b): parties, destination, ECCN, TPP, quantity, date. Taken from a transaction on the first of a 31-day month.
signals.doubt: 744 h is the minimum for the longest case; the 'first business day' slack (up to about 2-3 further days if the 1st falls on a weekend) is not added. Trigger is a transaction, coded 'schedule' because reports are monthly.

signals.receiver_name: the recipient of the export, reexport or transfer
signals.reasons: 'the exporter, reexporter, or transferor must inform the recipient that a BIS authorization is required' where use is at a data center giving access to more than 12,000,000 aggregate TPP for Macau or D:5 firms. No time is set.
signals.doubt: Trigger forced: the occasion is a transfer made without knowledge of the end use, which fits none of the values closely; 'event short of harm' chosen.

signals.reasons: Annual reports of reexporters or transferors using a VEU authorization: 'due by February 15 of each year, and must cover the period from January 1 through December 31 of the prior year'. Content: end-user name and address, destination, quantity, value, ECCN.
signals.doubt: Deadline taken from a 1 January transaction to the following 15 February in a leap year, 411 days = 9864 h (366 + 45 days); a clock of 'schedule' since the period is fixed.

extra.passage: shall describe the character and justification of the redaction in any published version of the document ... and shall retain the unredacted information for five years.
extra.why: A keep-for-five-years record duty for what was redacted from the framework, transparency report and similar published documents. Folded into CA1, CA2, NY1, NY2 as retention; listed in case the rule counts it apart.

extra.passage: frontier developers who comply with subdivision three of this section by meeting such federal standards shall send copies of any critical safety incident reports required by such federal standards to the office concurrently with sending them to federal authorities.
extra.why: A separate incident report to the office (deadline: concurrent with the federal report, 0 h from the federal filing), for developers using a designated federal law. No California counterpart in the text.

extra.passage: A frontier developer is encouraged, but not required, to report critical safety incidents pertaining to foundation models that are not frontier models.
extra.why: Incident report to the same office for non-frontier foundation models; only encouraged. Count depends on whether 'encouraged' counts as a duty; I code none.

extra.passage: you submit the following information to https://www.bis.gov/ai/exclusionnote submission, which will be shared with the End User Review Committee. (i) The name of the company ... (ii) The sum of the total processing performance ... (iii) The due diligence performed
extra.why: A submission to BIS of customer, compute and due-diligence information as condition for the commercial-recommender exception; no deadline; shared with the End User Review Committee.

extra.passage: Exporters, reexporters, and transferors shipping under VEU Authorization are required to provide the VEUs to which they are shipping notice of the shipment.
extra.why: A notice of shipment content (ECCNs, authorised contents) to the end user, within a timeframe agreed in writing; notifications are to be maintained under recordkeeping. A compute-kind notice to another party.

extra.passage: Certifications and all records relating to VEU must be retained by exporters, reexporters, or transferors in accordance with the recordkeeping requirements set forth in part 762
extra.why: A keep-records duty on compute transfers (also 744.24 records listed in 762.2); the retention period is in part 762, not in this text. Weak candidate.

signals.receiver_name: developers, service providers and special technical institutions (sharing mechanism)
signals.reasons: Covers 'vulnerabilities, defects, risks, threats, and safety incidents', so not harm-only; no deadline, no definition of what is shared.
signals.doubt: State-level 'we should'; who must feed the mechanism is unclear.

signals.receiver_name: unnamed body handling complaints and reports
signals.reasons: 'complaints and reports on AI risks and hazards' covers risks, not only harm.
signals.doubt: Receiver of the mechanism not named; coded other party as a fallback.

signals.reasons: 'generate detailed test reports' for 'products for commercial use'; no recipient or content definition.
signals.doubt: Recipient not stated; own record is a default. Timing 'before commercial use' inferred from commercial-use framing.

signals.reasons: 'inform service providers and other developers of its scope of application, precautions, or usage prohibitions'.
signals.doubt: Trigger not stated; placed in development phase (6.1 is developer guidance).

signals.reasons: 'Regularly disclose information on the auditing and anomaly handling'; no period number, so deadline none.
signals.doubt: Kind could be incident (anomaly handling); audit results taken as evaluation. Receiver unnamed, read as public.

signals.reasons: 'including system and user activities' separates system acts from user acts; 'retained for at least six months, and audited regularly'.
signals.doubt: machine_or_person: required read from the system/user split; could be not addressed.

signals.reasons: 'Set security alert thresholds for key operational indicators' is a monitoring setup, no stated record or report.
signals.doubt: May not be a signal at all: no record, report or receiver is required, only thresholds.

signals.reasons: 'disclosing their capabilities, limitations, target users, and scenarios'; no occasion given, read as continuous availability.
signals.doubt: Trigger not stated; kind evaluation is a best fit for capabilities and limitations.

signals.receiver_name: regulatory authorities, users, customers, value chain participants
signals.reasons: Incidents are failures or 'unintended harm' of 'sufficient severity'; 'when required or needed'; reporting tiered to severity.
signals.doubt: Unit: severity threshold is vague, could be named only. Receivers mixed; regulator placed first.

signals.reasons: 'transparency around safety best practices... relevant information to downstream deployers and end users'; disclosure level balanced against proprietary information.
signals.doubt: Kind and trigger uncertain (info on safety practices; timing implied by 'decisions about the deployment').

signals.receiver_name: the organization (reports by users and third parties)
signals.reasons: 'facilitating third-party and user discovery and reporting of issues and vulnerabilities after deployment'; vulnerabilities need no harm.
signals.doubt: Receiver is the organization itself; coded own record.

signals.reasons: 'publishing transparency reports... for all new significant releases'; contents listed (evaluations, capacities, risks, red-teaming results).

signals.receiver_name: other organizations developing advanced AI, and the public
signals.reasons: 'attempts by AI actors to circumvent safeguards' and 'dangerous intended or unintended capabilities'; 'share and report relevant information to the public'.
signals.doubt: Kind mixes incident and evaluation reports; AI actors include humans so not by class. Passage also names public authorities, listed as extra-2.

signals.reasons: 'establish and disclose their AI governance policies'; 'policies should also be regularly updated'.
'publish the non-sensitive findings of our evaluations in a standardized format'; 'publicly accessible shared repository'.
signals.doubt: No occasion stated; schedule is the nearest value. Only 'non-sensitive' findings, so a partial publication.

signals.reasons: 'Commit to disclose model capabilities, limitations, and known risks'; no recipient, timing or definition.
signals.doubt: Receiver not named, read as public; trigger not stated.

signals.receiver_name: government, other governments or other AI companies
signals.reasons: 'share timely information on serious cyber and AI control incidents and other material precursor signals of serious harm'; precursors need no harm; AI control incidents are the model's own conduct.
signals.doubt: 'timely' read as prompt, no number; clock unstated. Receiver mixes governments and companies; classification still to be aligned, so unit named only.

signals.reasons: 'concerns about systemic risks on reasonable grounds' needs no harm; channel is confidential.
signals.doubt: A commitment of policy makers, not developers; the receiving body is unnamed.

signals.reasons: 'real-time monitoring of emergent capabilities... transparent reporting lines that protect internal researchers'; internal.
signals.doubt: Bundles two contents (capability monitoring and internal reporting lines); only a recognition ('Recognize the importance'), no stated record.

signals.reasons: Records of 'decisions, actions, tool calls, inputs, outputs and human interventions' list human interventions as a field; retention appropriate, no number.

signals.receiver_name: the organization (receiver of the report not named)
signals.reasons: 'monitor for and report on unexpected behaviors or failures' of agents after deployment; behaviours are the system's own conduct.
signals.doubt: Receiver not stated; by class vs not addressed is a close call.

signals.reasons: 'up-to-date inventory of approved systems and their purposes, models, tools, skills, data sources, connections and permissions' lists the fields.
signals.doubt: Internal inventory of deployed systems, not a registration with a body.

extra.passage: Organizations are further encouraged to maintain appropriate documentation of reported incidents and to mitigate the identified risks and vulnerabilities, in collaboration with other stakeholders.
extra.why: Own-record log of reported incidents; distinct from the reporting channel in G7-1.

extra.passage: Organizations should also collaborate and share the aforementioned information with relevant public authorities, as appropriate.
extra.why: Same content as G7-3 but a different receiver (public authorities).

extra.passage: developers should seek to enable traceability, in relation to datasets, processes, and decisions made during system development. These measures should be documented and supported by regularly updated technical documentation.
extra.why: Own-record documentation of testing and development decisions; borderline.

extra.passage: Formulate rules for information content interaction, a secure operation mechanism, a complaint and feedback mechanism, and technical protection capabilities
extra.why: A complaint and feedback channel for users at the operator; kind channel.

extra.ref: China, Principle 6 of the governance principles
extra.passage: We should also conduct audits and maintain records throughout their full life cycle
extra.why: Own-record duty over the system's full life cycle; borderline, content not named.

extra.passage: The principles, capacities, application scenarios, and safety risks of AI technologies and products should be disclosed when necessary to make AI systems increasingly transparent.
extra.why: Disclosure of capacities and safety risks; overlaps CN8 but under another section and trigger ('when necessary').

extra.passage: organisations have policies and procedures for their employees to report incidents through proper channels, along with appropriate tools and training
extra.why: Internal incident-reporting channel, described as typical practice; borderline since the section is descriptive.

extra.passage: support the evaluation of models by qualified independent evaluators, as appropriate and consistent with existing practices and arrangements
extra.why: Access given to independent evaluators; kind compute (access); borderline.

extra.passage: establishing procedures to detect, investigate and respond to incidents; and updating relevant records following material changes.
extra.why: Own-record incident and change records; borderline since procedures rather than a record or report.

extra.passage: provide an accessible means to challenge the outcome and obtain meaningful review by a suitably qualified and authorized human decision-maker.
extra.why: A channel for persons to contest an agent's decision; borderline, review rather than report.
